Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 8. децембар ст. ст., „Свети апостоли Состен, Аполос, Тихик, Епафродит, Онисифор, Кифа и Кесар.“ — with «Свети апостоли» left off and the sixth of the seven bare forenames taken. `sr-foldpred.mjs` measured the folded string at 0 other holders, which is worth saying because Κηφάς is the name the Gospel gives Peter and the corpus holds eleven folders that share a bare «Петар»; this string folds with none of them.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 8 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The entry names all six of its members, so it is one folder per named member and each relates the others. Of this one the page says expressly «Τέλος, για τον Κηφά, δεν διασώζονται βιογραφικά του στοιχεία» — no biographical details of Cephas survive — so there is no see, no country and no year, and no `dates` object. The page's gloss that Κήφ or Κηφά is a Chaldean word meaning rock is its note on the name and carries no claim that this apostle is Peter. The one hymn on the page names Tychicus and is his. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 21.12.2025 (8. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети апостоли Состен, Аполос, Тихик, Епафродит, Онисифор, Кифа и Кесар.“

attestations.note: The sixth name of the day’s enumerated seven; the heading is quoted whole on each of the seven folders; URL year 2025. `types` UNTOUCHED: «апостоли» is the `apostle` held. NO `bishop` ADDED, AND IT IS THE SAME READING AS ON TYCHICUS: the entry seats him «у Иконији», in Iconium, in a sentence whose single verb «би епископ» governs only Sosthenes, and a see named without the rank word is not a rank this reader will write; the city is in the life. `dates` UNTOUCHED AND STILL ABSENT. THE BOOK’S OWN SECOND DAY FOR HIM, recorded and not acted on: «Кифа и Кесар 30. марта», Cephas and Caesar on 30 March, besides the 4 January on which it keeps all seven. One row per church is the schema, so this row records the day whose heading it quotes and the other days are named here; neither of them was read, and the Julian 30 March and 4 January are outside this reader’s range. NO `related` ROW ADDED: the other five of the Greek six are already here both ways. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
